name: HArmonyCa

card.summary: A hybrid injectable combining hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite that adds immediate lift and stimulates the skin to make collagen.
card.note: Prescription injectable given by clinicians; adverse events include injection-site reactions.

quick.overview:
HArmonyCa is an Allergan hybrid filler that suspends calcium hydroxyapatite (CaHA) microspheres in hyaluronic acid (HA) gel. It is used to lift and add volume to the face and improve skin quality.

The HA gives immediate fill, while CaHA stimulates the body to make collagen. Small clinical studies report volume gain and high patient satisfaction.
quick.how: A clinician injects it into the cheek and lower face with a cannula or needle; results are described as lasting months.
quick.risks: The most common adverse event is injection-site response; as with any filler, serious vascular events are possible and treatment should be done by qualified clinicians.

lead: HArmonyCa is a hybrid injectable filler from Allergan Aesthetics that contains calcium hydroxyapatite microspheres suspended in hyaluronic acid gel.[3] It is used for facial rejuvenation, lifting and volume restoration.
The HA gives an immediate filling and lifting effect, while CaHA microspheres drive neocollagenesis.[3] Preclinical data cited in one review showed higher lift capacity than a CaHA filler.[3]

chain: HA gel fills and lifts immediately
angle.text: Clinicians inject it to restore volume and tension in the cheeks and lower face, giving an immediate and then gradual lift.

paras: The product pairs a hyaluronic acid gel with CaHA microspheres, a mixture analysts have compared with other collagen-stimulating products.[3][6]

A prospective study of 15 patients injected in the preauricular region reported median volume gains of about 2.1 cc per side at day 180 and increased collagen on elastography.[1] An Italian real-life study of 129 patients reported physician-rated improvement for all patients at nine months.[2] A review pooled data showing safety and effectiveness with high satisfaction, with injection-site responses most common.[3] A 3D study of eight women measured volume gain and lifting.[4] A case report describes minimally invasive rejuvenation.[5]
